source_review.notes: Checked current official Linux kernel documentation for energy-aware scheduling, CPU frequency and idle management, the device energy model, power capping, thermal sysfs, runtime power management, system sleep, suspend interrupts, device PM dependencies and PM debugging. All eleven official URLs returned HTTP 200. Kernel interfaces, simplified energy models, empirical practices and broader engineering recommendations remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked power, energy, useful-work, shallow/deep power, transition energy, break-even time, exit latency, predicted-idle and effective-capacity notation.
Verified joule, watt, second and millisecond conversions and the condition P_shallow greater than P_deep.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes instantaneous or interval power, accumulated energy, work-normalized efficiency, platform estimates and service-latency constraints.

evidence: Recomputed break-even as 0.010 J divided by 3.5 W = 2.857 ms.
Recomputed shallow energy as 40 mJ, deep energy as 15 mJ, savings as 25 mJ, and 3 ms versus 1 ms latency eligibility.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic Python snippet reproduced every displayed value under the stated constant-power and fixed-transition-cost assumptions.

evidence: Derived the break-even inequality E_tr + P_deep*t no greater than P_shallow*t and solved t no less than E_tr/(P_shallow-P_deep).
Checked that energy eligibility and latency eligibility are conjunctive and neither implies platform correctness.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The derivation excludes entry duration, nonlinear leakage, domain coupling, prediction error and time-varying power; the chapter labels these limitations.

evidence: Reviewed short gaps, tight wake budgets, misprediction, domain coupling, burst demand, controller oscillation, counter wrap, thermal equilibrium, cap contention and low battery.
Reviewed suspend rollback, supplier ordering, wake storms, arriving I/O, sensor failure, hot removal, virtualization, measurement-boundary mismatch and loss of recovery capacity.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: CPU, scheduler, timer, thermal, cap, device, sleep, battery, measurement, fault and governance boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced workload observation through topology and capability discovery, cost estimation, feasible action, enforcement, service and energy measurement, then fallback.
Verified equal-work boundaries, domain coupling, lifecycle ordering, controller stability, sustained thermal safety, emergency degradation and exact-platform versioning.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariant set keeps optimization subordinate to correctness, service, thermal limits and authenticated recovery.

evidence: Reviewed fifteen objective, boundary, topology, capability, model, feasibility, selection, lifecycle, feedback, thermal, emergency, measurement, attribution, change and residual-risk obligations.
Constructed counterexamples for lower-power-as-lower-energy, frequency-as-performance, deepest-idle-as-best, race-to-idle-as-universal and component-counter-as-system-saving claims.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides conditional models and assurance obligations, not a proof of Linux policy optimality, hardware power, scheduler behavior or fleet-wide savings.

evidence: Audited uses of power, energy, capacity, optimal, break-even, predicted, eligible, efficient, savings, thermal and safe.
Confirmed hardware interfaces, model estimates, measured observations, policy recommendations and hard service constraints are labeled separately.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The toy energy comparison is never presented as a calibrated characterization of a real CPU, package, device or workload.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-098/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, Python toolchain and environment for the idle-state calculation.
Reviewed required wall and component energy, completed work, latency, frequency, residency, temperature, throttling, device, battery, counter-scope, calibration and rollback evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing snippet establishes six arithmetic and logical outputs only; it provides no evidence for real transition cost, power, idle prediction, exit latency, service or system energy.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed energy-aware operating systems as constrained feedback across workload, capacity, placement, performance state, idle residency, devices, thermal state and service outcomes.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including CPUFreq, CPUIdle, EAS, domains, timer coalescing, packing, thermal control, caps, runtime PM, system sleep, memory, devices, batteries, sensors, measurement, canaries and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from objective and work boundaries through CPU controls and placement to device lifecycle, coupled feedback, emergencies, evidence and governance, followed by fifteen obligations, fifteen trade-offs, twenty-six misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux power-management or scheduler maintainer, hardware energy-model specialist, thermal engineer, battery expert, device-driver practitioner, sustainability auditor, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
